name: Public Storage
description: Public Storage is the largest owner and operator of self-storage facilities in the United States: at Dec 31, 2025 it held interests in and consolidated 3,171 facilities (229 million net rentable square feet) in 40 states, operating under the Public Storage name. Customers rent storage units on a month-to-month basis for personal and business use, so the company earns rent that it can reprice frequently, and adds fees, merchandise (locks and boxes), tenant-insurance reinsurance, third-party management and, since 2024, bridge loans to third-party storage owners. It also owns 35 percent of Shurgard, a listed operator of 332 facilities in seven Western European countries, accounted for by the equity method. On July 22, 2026 it closed an all-stock merger with National Storage Affiliates Trust (NSA). Same-store revenue was flat in 2025 as softer demand lowered move-in rents and occupancy.

gics.note: Conventional label recorded from general knowledge of the standard scheme; not re-checked against an MSCI/S&P source in this pass. SEC SIC code is 6798 (Real Estate Investment Trusts). The box is close but hides that customers rent month to month, so rents reset continuously with demand (unlike triple-net landlords with long leases), that the company sells and reinsures tenant insurance (a small but higher-margin add-on), and that it owns 35 percent of a listed European operator, Shurgard.

hq.note: 2811 Internet Boulevard, Frisco, TX 75034 (Q2 2026 10-Q cover); incorporated in Maryland. The company was long based in Glendale, California; the cover page now shows Frisco.

employees.note: About 5,770 employees, including 4,920 in customer-facing roles (FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: Self-storage operations
businessLines.how: Customers pay monthly rent for a storage unit, month to month with no long lease, plus late and administrative fees; revenue depends on occupancy, the rate at which new tenants move in (often after a '$1 first month' promotion) and increases pushed through to existing tenants. Costs are mainly property taxes, on-site payroll and repairs.
businessLines.description: Owned and operated self-storage facilities in the U.S., reported as Same Store (2,565 facilities in 2025), Acquired, Newly Developed and Expanded, and Other Non-Same Store facilities.

operatingProfit.note: Net operating income computed here as segment revenue $4,489.4M less self-storage cost of operations $1,177.0M; Same Store NOI $2,828.9M (-0.5%)

businessLines.name: Ancillary operations
businessLines.how: A Public Storage subsidiary reinsures the tenant insurance policies (covering stored goods up to $5,000 per unit) and receives reinsurance premiums substantially equal to the premiums tenants pay a non-affiliated insurer; it also earns management fees on facilities it runs for others, retail margin on locks and boxes, and interest on bridge loans (three- or four-year terms, variable rate) to third-party owners.
businessLines.description: Tenant reinsurance, merchandise sales (locks and boxes), third-party self-storage property management, and a bridge-lending program launched in 2024.

operatingProfit.note: Computed: ancillary revenue $334.7M less ancillary cost of operations $132.9M

businessLines.name: Investment in Shurgard Self Storage Limited (35 percent, equity method)
businessLines.how: Not consolidated: Public Storage records its 35 percent share of Shurgard's earnings and receives dividends; Shurgard's rent model is the same month-to-month self-storage rent.
businessLines.description: Public company on Euronext Brussels (SHUR) that owns and operates 332 self-storage facilities (18 million net rentable sq ft) in seven Western European countries under the Shurgard name (Dec 31, 2025).
